name: No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas

ingredients.buy: 12 oz (2 1/3 of the 5.2 oz packages), crumbled
1 lb 4 oz drained (about 2 1/3 cans), roughly chopped
2 1/3 tsp finely grated (zest of the same lemons)

writer_notes: Source is a single 9x13 at ~6 servings; scaled ~2.333x to 14 servings, so method directs splitting across two 9x13 dishes or one large roaster. Ingredients unchanged, vessel guidance only.
No cost_lines were provided in this dispatch, so no per-ounce or per-package savings claims were made; all money uses the ${{cost_ps}} token.
Macros written as {{cal}}/{{protein}} tokens per templated-catalog convention; locked view shows 603 cal and 54.8 g protein per serving.
All 13 bought lines are consumed by a step (parmesan in bake step, parsley in garnish step); no orphaned ingredients and no unbought items used.
Boursin is called for crumbled from the 5.2 oz packages; parmesan specified freshly grated to melt into the top, matching the source.

prose.intro_html:
Here is a weeknight truth: the fewer pots you dirty, the more likely you are to actually cook. This no-boil chicken pasta casserole is a dump-and-bake, which means the penne goes in dry, the sauce goes over the top, and the oven does the boiling for you. No colander, no steamy kitchen, no second pan waiting in the sink.

What makes it worth your time is the sauce. Cottage cheese and Boursin go into a blender with garlic, lemon, and salt until they are silky, and that turns into a creamy blanket that reads like a fussy restaurant bake without the fuss. Artichoke hearts and sweet peas keep it from feeling heavy, and the chicken breast carries the protein. At {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, this is a real dinner, not a side dish pretending to be one.
prose.shop_smart:
This is a batch build for fourteen containers, so shop it like one. Grab your penne by the box, and use plain penne rather than a specialty shape so the dry pasta cooks evenly under the sauce. Chicken breast is easiest to buy as a family pack and cube it yourself into one-inch pieces at home.

The sauce leans on two dairy items. Cottage cheese comes in a tub, and Boursin comes in the small 5.2 ounce foil packages, so plan on the count the card calls for. Freshly grated parmesan matters here because the recipe asks for it grated fine to melt into a golden top, so buy a wedge and grate it yourself rather than reaching for anything pre-shredded.

Frozen peas are your friend for a batch this size since you scoop exactly what you need and the rest goes back in the freezer. Canned artichoke hearts just need a good draining and a rough chop. Round it out with a couple of lemons for both juice and zest, a head of garlic, and a little fresh parsley or basil for the garnish at the end.
prose.make_it:
Heat the oven to 400 degrees. Lightly grease your baking vessels and set them aside. A quick heads up on size: this is a fourteen-serving batch, so it will not fit one 9x13 dish. Split it across two greased 9x13 dishes or use one large roasting pan, and keep the layers even so everything cooks at the same pace.

Make the sauce in a blender or food processor. Combine the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt, and blend until completely smooth. Pour in the chicken broth and blend again until the sauce is silky and fully combined. It will look very thin, and that is exactly right, because the dry pasta is going to drink it up in the oven.

Now assemble. Spread the dry penne across the bottom of your greased dishes, then scatter the cubed chicken, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Pour the blended sauce over everything, and make sure the pasta is fully submerged. Any noodle poking out will not cook, so nudge them down.

Cover each dish tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Pull them out, take off the foil, and give everything a good stir. The pasta should be just shy of done at this point. Top with the freshly grated parmesan and return to the oven uncovered for another 5 to 10 minutes, bumping the heat up if you want the top golden. If the pasta already feels al dente, skip straight to the parmesan.

Let the finished bake rest at least 10 minutes before you touch it. That rest lets the sauce set up so it clings to the pasta instead of running. Finish with the chopped parsley or basil, and it is ready to portion.
prose.portion_html:
Do not eyeball this one. The honest way to hit fourteen even servings is to weigh the pot. Set your empty storage container on the scale and zero it out, weigh the full finished casserole, subtract the container weight, and divide that number by fourteen. That gram figure is your target scoop for each container.

Fill each one to that weight and you get fourteen identical dinners, every one landing at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein. Cool them, lid them, and they stack neat in the fridge for the week. A creamy pasta bake reheats best with a splash of water or broth stirred in before it goes in the microwave, which loosens the sauce right back up.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is where the dump-and-bake pays you back. One batch of this casserole is fourteen full dinners, and it lands at ${{cost_ps}} a serving. That is a creamy, protein-heavy meal for the price of a drive-through soda, and you made all fourteen at once instead of deciding what is for dinner fourteen separate times.

Run the math on your week. Fourteen servings at ${{cost_ps}} each is your whole lunch-and-dinner problem solved for a fraction of what takeout costs, and the only tax you paid was twenty minutes of assembly and an hour of oven time you spent doing something else.

head.description: A no-boil dump-and-bake chicken pasta casserole with artichokes and peas in a creamy cottage cheese and Boursin sauce. One batch makes 14 high-protein meal-prep dinners.
head.keywords: no boil chicken pasta casserole, dump and bake pasta, chicken artichoke casserole, high protein meal prep, cottage cheese pasta bake, Boursin pasta, budget meal prep dinner, penne casserole
steps: Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease your baking vessels. For this 14-serving batch use two 9x13 dishes or one large roasting pan and set aside.

In a blender or food processor, blend the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt until smooth. Add the chicken broth and blend again until silky. The sauce will look very thin, which is correct.

Spread the dry penne across the bottom of the greased dishes. Scatter the cubed chicken, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over the pasta, then pour the blended sauce over everything and press any pasta down so it is fully submerged.
Cover each dish tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Remove the foil and stir well; the pasta should be slightly undercooked.
Top with the freshly grated parmesan and return uncovered to the oven for 5 to 10 minutes, raising the heat if needed to brown the top.
Rest at least 10 minutes so the sauce sets, then garnish with chopped parsley or basil, portion into 14 containers, and serve.
